text:
Joe H: Heads-up — OptiCart on dedicated pool dc-optic-prod is seeing repeated latency spikes and 429s since 06:12 UTC. Customer says their checkout queue spiked and the pool bounced 3x in ~8m. Attaching quick logs: https://redwood.internal/echo/optic/logs/2987654321
Support Bot: Ticket #CS-9142 created, customer-reported error samples attached. They reported throttling errors and slow tail latency.
Anya R: I see autoscaler activity for that pool: scale_up -> scale_down -> scale_up pattern. Looks like queue length crosses threshold then quickly drops (maybe short bursts) causing churn.
Kevin M: Can you paste the autoscaler events? Also any noisy tenant running cron?
Joe H: events: `scale_up @06:13 (+4 GPUs)`, `scale_down @06:15 (-4)`, `scale_up @06:20 (+4)`. Metrics show request rate spiking to 180 TPS for 30-60s, then back to 10 TPS.
Liz K: That short spike duration will definitely trigger our proportional scaler. Cooldown is 120s currently, threshold is queue>50. If spikes are short, we oscillate.
Anya R: Agree. Also noticed `vm_cpu_util` for pool drops right after scale_up — looks like new nodes join but requests already finished.
Kevin M: Repro attempt — I can replay a synthetic burst from staging to validate hysteresis. Using hey: `hey -n 2000 -c 400 https://dc-optic-prod.redwood/api/generate`.
Joe H: Before we run: quick telemetry queries: `sum(rate(pool_requests[1m])) by (pool)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,pool))`. Share results if you run.
Anya R: Running queries now — 06:12–06:22 window shows 3 short peaks ~40–70s each. P95 latency jumps from 120ms to 1.1s during peaks.
Autoscale Bot: Autoscaler event: pool=dc-optic-prod action=scale_up reason=queue>50 new_capacity=12 at=2026-03-17T06:13:04Z
Liz K: Quick mitigation suggestion: bump cooldown to 300s for this pool and add a rate-based smoothing window (moving average 2m) so scaler reacts to sustained load not blips.
Kevin M: For immediate relief we can temporarily increase threshold to queue>120 and increase cooldown to 300s. That will let transient spikes pass without adding nodes.
Joe H: Customer wants a fix ASAP — can we apply temporary config? If so we'll notify and monitor.
Anya R: I'll patch the pool policy: `patch /pools/dc-optic-prod` payload: `{"scaler": {"cooldown_secs":300, "queue_threshold":120, "smoothing_window_secs":120}}` — applying in 1m.
Support Bot: Notifying OptiCart support contact that we're applying a temporary config change and will monitor for 30m.
Autoscale Bot: Config change applied for pool=dc-optic-prod by Anya R at 2026-03-17T06:25:10Z
Liz K: After change we should watch for underprovisioning if they do sustained load. Keep an eye on 5m avg CPU and queue.
Kevin M: I'll start a synthetic burst loop in staging to simulate the pattern and test tuned cooldown/gain.
Joe H: Post-change live readouts: queue peaks now cause no scale events in first 30m and p95 latency stays ~200ms. Customer reports tail latency improved and fewer 429s.
Anya R: We'll follow up with a permanent policy: consider using rate-based autoscaling (GPU workers per sustained qps) + tenant burst protection (burst buckets) and add a smoothing adapter in the scaler.
Liz K: Filed follow-up RFC: RFC-ops-718 (autoscaler smoothing & tenant burst mitigation). Assigning to eng-sre + eng-platform.
Joe H: Thanks all — marking thread resolved for customer; keep monitoring and reopen if we see recurrence. :white_check_mark:
